sources.citation: W3C, Understanding SC 1.4.1 Use of Color, WCAG 2.2
sources.shows: Colour may not be the only visual means; a lightness difference of 3:1 counts as a visual means.
sources.doesNotShow: Does not address diffs specifically.

sources.citation: W3C, Understanding SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
sources.shows: 3:1 for graphics required to understand content and focus indicators; text glyphs used as symbols count as non-text; decorative or redundant graphics are exempt.
sources.doesNotShow: Does not rule on diff tints; the redundancy reading is mine.

sources.citation: W3C, Understanding SC 1.4.10 Reflow
sources.shows: Code indentation is named as layout that can carry meaning and qualify for the two-dimensional exception.
sources.doesNotShow: Not a mandate to scroll; says nothing about tints.

sources.citation: W3C, Understanding SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
sources.shows: A focused component must not be entirely hidden by author content; refers to 2.4.7.
sources.doesNotShow: Text of 2.4.7 itself not read.

sources.citation: W3C, Understanding SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions
sources.shows: Level AAA; prefers-reduced-motion is a named technique.
sources.doesNotShow: AAA, not required by AA.

sources.citation: MDN, forced-colors media feature
sources.shows: Forced colours overrides color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color; box-shadow, text-shadow and non-URL background-image go to none.
sources.doesNotShow: Does not say which engines trigger it on which OS setting.

sources.citation: W3C, CSS Color Adjustment Module Level 1, CR Snapshot 2026-05-07
sources.shows: Defines forced colours mode and forced-color-adjust.
sources.doesNotShow: Details of background-color alpha handling not verified.

sources.citation: mdn/browser-compat-data issue 27143, 2025-06-25
sources.shows: Reporter found macOS Increase Contrast does not activate forced-colors in Safari.
sources.doesNotShow: One tester, one issue, Safari not WKWebView-in-Tauri; not a WebKit statement.

sources.citation: MDN, prefers-contrast
sources.shows: Values no-preference/more/less/custom; Baseline since May 2022; reads OS setting.
sources.doesNotShow: Whether WKWebView inside Tauri reports it was not tested.

sources.citation: GitHub Primer primitives 11.10.0 (MIT), diffBlob tokens and built theme CSS
sources.shows: The official diff line and word colours per theme including colour-blind variants.
sources.doesNotShow: Only the five prettylights syntax colours were sampled as text.

sources.citation: GitHub Changelog, Protanopia & Deuteranopia Colorblind Themes Beta, 2022-04-19
sources.shows: The single colour-blind theme was split into Protanopia & Deuteranopia and Tritanopia.
sources.doesNotShow: No user-outcome data.

sources.citation: Microsoft VS Code (MIT), theme-defaults themes and editorColors.ts
sources.shows: Default diffEditor inserted/removed line and text colours.
sources.doesNotShow: Only comment and constant.language tokens sampled; 2026 Light line fallback assumed.

sources.citation: Machado, Oliveira, Fernandes, A Physiologically-based Model for Simulation of Color Vision Deficiency, IEEE TVCG 15(6), 2009
sources.depth: paper PDF (text read by skeptic pass)
sources.shows: Matrices confirmed against authors' page; FM100H validation reported; paper declines to model tritanopia (tritanomaly by shift only).
sources.doesNotShow: Not stated whether matrices apply to linear RGB.

sources.citation: colour-science machado2010.py (BSD-3-Clause)
sources.shows: Severity-1.0 matrices used in the simulation.
sources.doesNotShow: Docstring cites the 2010 thesis; values equal the authors' published ones.

sources.citation: Ottosson, A perceptual color space for image processing, 2020
sources.shows: OKLab definition and matrices, public domain or MIT.
sources.doesNotShow: Gives no just-noticeable-difference threshold I could verify.

sources.citation: Okabe and Ito, Color Universal Design, 2002/2008
sources.shows: Avoid red-green pairs, use lightness differences and redundant cues.
sources.doesNotShow: Design guidance, not a reader test.

sources.citation: GitHub Docs, Basic writing and formatting syntax (Alerts)
sources.shows: Five alert types; rendered with distinctive colours and icons; use sparingly.
sources.doesNotShow: No evidence alerts help readers.

sources.citation: Adrian Roselli, Tweaking Text Level Styles, 2017 (updated 2024)
sources.shows: NVDA announces ins/del; JAWS rolled back; mark is announced differently across readers; generated-content workaround is verbose.
sources.doesNotShow: Versions and dates of the tested screen readers not verified.

sources.citation: W3C, WAI-ARIA 1.2, roles log/insertion/deletion
sources.shows: log is for sequentially updated content; insertion and deletion roles exist.
sources.doesNotShow: Implicit aria-live value not read (summary truncated).

sources.citation: W3C, ARIA Authoring Practices: Disclosure pattern
sources.shows: Button with aria-expanded, operated by Enter and Space.
sources.doesNotShow: A pattern, not a reader study.

sources.citation: W3C, CSS Color Module Level 4 (gamut mapping: JND as OkLCh distance 0.02)
sources.shows: One JND is an OkLCh difference of 0.02 (2 in x100 units).
sources.doesNotShow: Not a reading-task or dichromat threshold.

gaps.what: Four diff tint colours as theme tokens
gaps.detail: Frozen token set (ADR-0008); nothing exists for diff backgrounds and a theme cannot set what is not a token
gaps.proposal: ADR adding --marxy-color-diff-add, -diff-del, -diff-add-word, -diff-del-word with the dark and light defaults in the chapter; registry entries first

gaps.detail: scopes.ts maps twelve classes and markup.inserted/deleted to none; class and data-attribute names must be in scripts/registry.json
gaps.proposal: Add line-level classes to the registry and a line-prefix pass on .marxy-line, rather than token classes
Registry entry and one class, as chapter 03 proposes

gaps.what: Contrast gate over every text-on-tint pair
gaps.detail: gate:aesthetics does not know diff tints exist
gaps.proposal: Extend the mechanical contrast check to compose each diff token over the code ground and test the twelve classes plus text and secondary

gaps.detail: base.css has none; not frozen, so a story rather than an ADR
gaps.proposal: Add rules in base.css and a CSS lint test

stories.summary: Tint added and removed diff lines and changed words
stories.why: Diffs are a first-class artifact and today are uncoloured
acceptance: 1. New packages/theme test composes each diff token over the code ground and asserts every token class and the code text is at least 4.5:1 on all four tints in dark and light.
2. Same test asserts the added/removed line pair differs in OKLab L by at least 0.05 and in OKLab ΔE by at least 4 under protan, deutan and tritan simulation.
3. gate:golden updated for the new line classes; gate:fidelity unchanged.
stories.tasteRow: Before/after of a real diff in dark and light at the corpus 16-api-reference and a PR diff. Question: does the raised-added, resting-removed asymmetry read correctly, and is the dark removed tint too brown?

stories.summary: Keep every cue readable under increased contrast and forced colours
stories.why: Tints vanish in forced colours; markers, borders and outlines must carry the meaning
acceptance: 1. New CSS lint test fails if any diff, fold or change-mark rule conveys state through background-color alone.
2. A test loads base.css with prefers-contrast: more emulated and asserts the diff border rule applies.

stories.summary: Make fold controls real buttons with a visible focus ring
stories.why: Keyboard and screen-reader access to summoned folds
acceptance: 1. New unit test asserts a fold control is a button with aria-expanded and toggles on Enter and Space.
2. New test asserts no transition or animation property applies to expand or collapse.

taste: Whether a raised added line and a resting removed line reads as intended, or whether readers expect matched weight
Whether the dark removed tint (hue 40, chroma 0.044) looks brown rather than red
Whether the light word tint is visible enough at ΔE 1.8 to 2.9 from its line tint
Whether amber comment text on the brown-red removed tint reads as two meanings
changeMyMind: A reader study showing lightness-only pairs slow or confuse diff reading would reverse the lightness-first design
A reading-task threshold well above DeltaE 4 (the CSS Color 4 JND is 2) would fail the light theme's protan line pair (4.7)
Evidence that type-coloured alerts improve comprehension would reopen no-hue alerts
WKWebView reporting forced-colors would make the forced-colors rules first-class rather than defensive
